- `src/ports.rs`: The bridge's ports and what each carries (features/network.md, Networks): an Ethernet port is a trunk (the untagged network untagged, every network with a VLAN tagged) unless the node's port profile says otherwise; a port that carries nothing leaves the bridge.
- `src/preserve.rs`: Values the node generated for itself, carried over from its current packages: they are the node's, not the site's, and losing them would change it.
- `src/raw.rs`: A node's raw sections (the validated escape hatch, D-011): each joins its package after everything rendered, or replaces the rendered section of the same name; a merge (D-072) sets its options on a rendered section instead, found by name or, for an anonymous one, by the key options of its type ([`key`]).
- `src/redirect.rs`: The gateway's port forwards and DMZ host as fw4 `redirect`s (features/network.md, Firewall policy): DNAT from the WAN to the zone of the network whose subnet holds the host. fw4 accepts what it forwards, and reflects it to the networks (NAT reflection) unless a forward says otherwise.
- `src/roaming.rs`: A WLAN's roaming options on each of its BSSes (features/wifi.md, Roaming; D-085), each only where the node's hostapd has it: 802.11r (fast transition) over the air in the WLAN's mobility domain, its PMK-R0/R1 keys generated locally for WPA2 or, for SAE, sent between the access points under the WLAN's FT key ([`Secrets::ft_key`](crate::Secrets::ft_key)); 802.11k neighbor reports (the controller fills them in, M5.2); 802.11v BSS transition with WNM sleep, its keys left out of sleep responses for stations that would reinstall them.
- `src/split.rs`: Splitting a node's `network` package into the WAN and the rest, so an apply that changes the WAN with other things can change it last, in its own transaction (features/lifecycle.md, Make-before-break; D-081).
- `src/sqm.rs`: The `sqm` package (features/wan.md, SQM; D-076): one `queue` that shapes the WAN's layer-3 device with cake through sqm-scripts' `piece_of_cake.qos`, a little below the line's rates, with fairness per host behind NAT.
- `src/switch.rs`: A swconfig switch in the `network` package: one `switch_vlan` per network (each user port as its profile says: by default untagged in the untagged network, tagged in the others) and on the gateway one for the WAN, each tagged on its CPU port, whose `<cpu>.<vid>` devices netifd then creates.
- `src/system.rs`: The `system` package: the node's hostname, time zone and NTP.
- `src/upnp.rs`: The `upnpd` package (miniupnpd; features/network.md, Firewall policy; D-079): UPnP IGD and NAT-PMP/PCP for the chosen networks, in secure mode (a client maps ports only to itself), with OpenWrt's stock permissions (ports from 1024 only) and lease file, which the agent's `leases` set reads for the live mappings.
- `src/usteer.rs`: The `usteer` package (features/wifi.md, Steering & balancing; D-090): usteer on each node that carries a steered WLAN, set by the site's profile, exchanging what it sees with the other nodes' over the management network (UDP 16720, which that network's zone accepts).
- `src/wan.rs`: The gateway's uplink in the `network` package (features/wan.md, Rendering on the gateway): the WAN device (an ISP's VLAN with its 802.1p priority, a cloned or the board's MAC, the MTU), `wan` by DHCP, static, PPPoE or DS-Lite, and `wan6` by DHCPv6 with prefix delegation or by 6rd.
- `src/wireless.rs`: The `wireless` package: a `wifi-device` per radio (its channel, width and power from the band's policy and the node's overrides, within what its phy supports), each WLAN's `wifi-iface` on every radio of its bands (`uw_<wlan>_<band>`, features/wifi.md), and the mesh point.
- `tests/backhaul.rs`: The wired backhaul (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-094): batman-adv over a cable on the backhaul VLAN, beside the networks (overlay) or alone (exclusive), and the cables a node can't give it.
- `tests/golden.rs`: Golden tests (docs/dev/TESTING.md): each role × feature × capability set renders into a snapshot under `tests/snapshots/`.
- `tests/steering.rs`: Steering (features/wifi.md, Steering & balancing; D-090): usteer's package per profile, where it runs, and what is left when steering goes off.
- `tests/support/mod.rs`: Inputs for the golden tests: the canonical gateway's facts and variants of it for each capability set, a home site, its secrets, and OpenWrt's stock packages as a node's current ones.

### `uniwrt-rf` (crates/rf)

RF insight (features/wifi.md, RF insight): what the site's radios hear and how crowded their channels are, from the nodes' facts and their radios' neighbor scans; later the channel planner (M6.1).

- `src/build.rs`: Building the [`RfReport`] from the nodes' facts, their radios' latest scans and the radar history.
- `src/lib.rs`: RF insight (features/wifi.md, RF insight): what the site's radios hear and how crowded their channels are, from the nodes' facts and their radios' neighbor scans; later the channel planner (M6.1).
- `src/radar.rs`: Radar hits from hostapd's log (`DFS-RADAR-DETECTED`, the `dfs-radar` pattern): where the radar was, so each channel's radar history can be told.
- `src/report.rs`: The RF report: per band, the site's radios, each channel's occupancy, the networks heard and the inter-node RSSI matrix.
- `src/span.rs`: The frequencies a channel occupies, how much two channels share, and how much a signal counts.
- `src/tests.rs`: A small site made in code: node 1 and node 2, each with a 5 GHz radio on channel 36 at 80 MHz carrying an AP and a mesh point, and node 1's latest scan.

### `uniwrt` (crates/server)

The `uniwrt` binary: CLI, configuration and composition root; serves the API and the web UI.

- `build/civil.rs`: Dependency-free UTC date formatting, shared by the build script and the crate's unit tests.
- `build/main.rs`: Build script: the build identity (`meta`) and the embedded web UI (`ui`), written to `$OUT_DIR`.
- `build/meta.rs`: Build identity: `$OUT_DIR/build_info.rs` with the version, commit, build time and target.
- `build/ui.rs`: Embeds the web UI: every file plus brotli and gzip variants, and a lookup table sorted by path (`$OUT_DIR/ui.rs`, included by `src/ui/assets.rs`).
- `src/autotune.rs`: SQM's autotune (features/wan.md, SQM; D-076): with autotune on in the latest revision, a test of the line (SQM bypassed) once a week in the site's night, kept in the history.
- `src/build_info.rs`: Build identity from build/meta.rs: the version and commit (injected by CI), the build time and the target triple.
- `src/cli.rs`: Command-line interface.
- `src/controller_key.rs`: The controller's SSH key: generated on the first run and kept in the vault (features/adoption.md, Identity, credentials, trust).
- `src/demo.rs`: Demo mode's adoptions: [`DemoDial`] reaches the simulated nodes as [`SshDial`] reaches real ones, so the real adopt job and discovery run against them.
- `src/demo_backhaul_tests.rs`: The wired backhaul end to end in demo mode (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-097): the demo's plain cable between the living room's and the office's access points, both managed, comes over as an overlay in the first transaction, passes the probe from both ends, and carries the mesh alone after the backhaul round.
- `src/demo_site.rs`: Demo mode's first revision (D-071, D-073): the brownfield import of the simulated nodes it adopted (their facts and `/etc/config` as they hold them, which `POST v1/import/preview` reads too) into the defaults, named "Demo home".
- `src/fleet.rs`: The fleet at startup: an SSH link per adopted node, handed to the engine with the node's latest snapshot, the snapshot writer, the topology's history, the metrics recorder, the clients' recorder (which restores the clients first) and the log recorder (with the syslog receiver, when it listens); the event recorder, the notifications, the alert engine and RF insight's scanner join them once the job runner is up ([`Fleet::record_events`]; demo mode scans sooner and busy or not).
- `src/fleet_link.rs`: [`FleetLink`]: the one link type the engine runs on, so the API has one engine type whether the nodes are real (SSH) or simulated (demo mode).
- `src/healthcheck.rs`: `uniwrt healthcheck`: `GET /api/v1/health` on the local server; success means a 200.
- `src/http/mod.rs`: The HTTP surface: the API (`uniwrt-api`) under `/api`, the embedded UI as the fallback, and the middleware both share.
- `src/http/plain.rs`: The plain HTTP listener (features/security.md, TLS; D-039): it redirects to HTTPS, except for the health check (Docker probes it) and for requests from a trusted reverse proxy, which terminates TLS itself and gets the whole application.
- `src/logging.rs`: Logging: `tracing` to stderr, filtered by `--log` / `UNIWRT_LOG` (`EnvFilter` syntax).
- `src/main.rs`: The `uniwrt` binary: CLI, configuration and composition root; serves the API and the web UI.
- `src/master_key.rs`: The vault's master key (features/security.md, Secrets vault): from `UNIWRT_MASTER_KEY`, or from its file (`<data dir>/master.key` unless `--master-key-file` says otherwise), which the first run creates with mode 0600.
- `src/recollect.rs`: Fresh facts after a wpad swap (D-089): the node's capabilities change, which the engine collects hourly, so the job's end has it collect every set again at once.
- `src/serve.rs`: `uniwrt serve`: starts the runtime, opens the database and the vault, binds the HTTP and HTTPS listeners and serves until SIGTERM or SIGINT.
- `src/tls/issue.rs`: Issuing the controller's certificates with rcgen (D-039): the local CA ([`Ca`]: ECDSA P-256, 10 years, no intermediates, name-constrained) and the leaf it signs for the HTTPS listener ([`Leaf`]: 397 days, server authentication only).
- `src/tls/issue/tests.rs`: Certificates checked as a client checks them: webpki, with the CA as the only root.
- `src/tls/listener.rs`: [`TlsListener`]: TLS on top of a TCP listener, as an axum [`Listener`]; [`PlainListener`], the HTTP listener's; and [`Peer`], the client's address that handlers on either listener extract with `ConnectInfo<Peer>`.
- `src/tls/mod.rs`: HTTPS (features/security.md, TLS; D-039): the controller's local CA and the leaf it signs, kept in the vault, served by rustls on the HTTPS listener and renewed while running.
- `src/tls/names.rs`: The names the controller's certificate covers ([`Names`]), and where its local CA may sign names at all ([`Permitted`], the CA's name constraints; D-039).
- `src/tls/tests.rs`: [`start`] and the [`Renewer`] over a real vault, on a manual clock.
- `src/ui/assets.rs`: The asset table: one entry per UI file, each with optional brotli and gzip variants.
- `src/ui/encoding.rs`: `Accept-Encoding` negotiation (RFC 9110 §12.5.3) over the variants an asset has.
- `src/ui/mod.rs`: The embedded web UI: the asset table generated by build/ui.rs, `Accept-Encoding` negotiation and the SPA fallback.
- `src/ui/respond.rs`: Answers a UI request with an embedded file, the SPA page for a client-side route, or a 404.
- `src/version.rs`: `uniwrt version`: build information as text or JSON.

### `uniwrt-sim` (crates/sim)

The simulated fleet: a gateway, mesh access points and their clients, each node behind a [`NodeLink`](uniwrt_node::NodeLink) that speaks the agent's protocol, for demo mode (`uniwrt serve --demo`) and tests.

- `src/brownfield.rs`: The simulated fleet as a brownfield (features/lifecycle.md, Brownfield import): each node's facts, as its agent reports them, and its `/etc/config` before uniwrt manages it (`render::config`), for import's round-trip tests and the demo.
- `src/fleet.rs`: [`SimFleet`]: the world, a link per node, and the driver task that advances the world one second per second of tokio's clock.
- `src/hand_edit.rs`: Drift in the demo (features/lifecycle.md, Drift; D-074): a minute after a node's first confirmed apply, someone changes one option of a package that apply wrote, as `LuCI` saves it (the file parsed and written back as `uci commit` does), once per node.
- `src/isp.rs`: The simulated ISP behind the gateway's WAN port (features/wan.md; D-075): like Lumen's fiber, it serves DHCP on VLAN 201, delegates a /56 over DHCPv6 on it, and runs a 6rd border relay.
- `src/lib.rs`: The simulated fleet: a gateway, mesh access points and their clients, each node behind a [`NodeLink`](uniwrt_node::NodeLink) that speaks the agent's protocol, for demo mode (`uniwrt serve --demo`) and tests.
- `src/line.rs`: The ISP's line as the speed test meets it (features/wan.md, SQM; D-076): a 500/100 Mbit/s fiber tier whose buffers bloat under load unless the gateway shapes below its rates.
- `src/link.rs`: [`SimLink`]: one simulated node behind [`NodeLink`].
- `src/link/backhaul.rs`: The wired backhaul's `mtu` op (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-096), as `node-agent/mtu.uc` answers it: the device's MTU and the link-local addresses that answered the probe's size, from the cables' ends as each node's `network` sets them ([`World::probe`]).
- `src/link/steering.rs`: The ops steering sends (features/wifi.md, Steering & balancing; D-093): `btm`, as `node-agent/btm.uc` has hostapd send a transition request, and `ubus` for usteer's `get_client_info`, the one call the controller makes through it.
- `src/render/batman.rs`: The `batman` set: batctl's JSON for bat0 (mesh info, hard interfaces, originators, neighbors, gateways, translation tables).
- `src/render/cable_tests.rs`: The demo's plain cable through the node crate's parsers and the topology: bridged at both ends it is a wired link; the hard interfaces an apply adds on its VLAN carry batman-adv once both ends have them, and the `mtu` probe passes where both ends take 1532 bytes.
- `src/render/commands.rs`: The commands the jobs run on a node, answered as OpenWrt would: adoption's (features/adoption.md, Path A: `/etc/openwrt_release`, the script that appends the controller's key to dropbear's `authorized_keys`, the package manager's database (opkg's status file, or apk's installed database and world file) and `sysupgrade -b -`), the transaction tool's and the reads of the current configuration ([`crate::txn`], D-069), and the gateway's DNS check (`nslookup`).
- `src/render/config.rs`: A node's `/etc/config` before uniwrt manages it: OpenWrt 25.12's stock packages, configured by hand to run the simulated network (the gateway's LAN, WAN on VLAN 201 and DHCP; the access points as bridges taking their address over DHCP, dnsmasq, odhcpd and the firewall off; the sim's SSID on both bands and its batman-adv mesh on 5 GHz), so that the demo's review shows what managing such a fleet changes.
- `src/render/devices.rs`: The `devices` set: each kernel device's sysfs attributes, and its counters in /proc/net/dev.
- `src/render/feeds.rs`: The package feeds as an apply's install step meets them (D-076): `opkg update` / `apk update`, then installing what SQM, failover, UPnP and steering need, which brings their init scripts (enabled, as postinst scripts do) and their stock `/etc/config` files; and the init scripts' `start`, `stop`, `enable` and `disable`.
- `src/render/l2.rs`: The sets `leases` (dnsmasq's lease file, odhcpd's ubus leases and, where the gateway runs miniupnpd, its lease file) and `neighbors` (the ARP and NDP caches and the bridge's forwarding database over rtnetlink).
- `src/render/logs.rs`: `log` batches as the agent pushes them: logd's entries when polled, or `logread -f -t` lines when streamed (`<ctime> [<secs>.<ms>] <facility>.<severity> <msg>`).
- `src/render/mod.rs`: Rendering the world as a node's agent reports it: every collect set in the raw shapes of `node-agent/collect/` ([`collect`]), the hello, hostapd's and dnsmasq's notifications, and log batches in both of `log_follow`'s modes, and the `scan` op's answer.
- `src/render/net.rs`: The `interfaces` set: netifd's `network.interface dump`.
- `src/render/scan.rs`: The `scan` op's answer in the agent's raw shape (`node-agent/scan.uc`): the networks next door (a fixed set outside the house), the other nodes' access points and mesh points (an unadopted one too), each at the signal the path between them leaves, with their information elements; and the channel survey of the band, busier where networks crowd.
- `src/render/system.rs`: The sets `board`, `system` and `capabilities`, shaped as `node-agent/collect/` sends them: ubus `system board` and `system info`, `/etc/openwrt_release`, board.json, thermal zones.
- `src/render/tests.rs`: Every rendered set and push, through the node crate's parsers: what a simulated node reports must read as a real one's does, and agree with the world.
- `src/render/wifi.rs`: The sets `radios` (netifd's wireless status, nl80211 interfaces and surveys), `stations` (nl80211 station dumps and hostapd's clients) and `phys` (a two-band MT7986, from the hwsim capture's wiphys).
- `src/render/wpad.rs`: The node's wpad and the wpad swap's commands (D-089).
- `src/rng.rs`: [`Rng`]: `xoshiro256**` seeded through `SplitMix64`.
- `src/txn.rs`: The transaction tool as a node runs it (`node-agent/txn/txn`; features/lifecycle.md, Render → diff → apply, D-069), with the node's `/etc/config` files and init scripts: the simulated fleet runs it, and the jobs' tests drive it through their scripted nodes.
- `src/txn/tests.rs`: The simulated tool answers the node crate's commands as the real one does.
- `src/world/cables.rs`: The cables between nodes other than the gateway's batman-adv uplink ([`Node::wired`]): plain Ethernet that each end bridges into its LAN until the controller brings it over to the wired backhaul (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-094).
- `src/world/catalog.rs`: What the simulated fleet is made of: hardware models, firmware releases, the house's places and the kinds of client, each with how it moves, what it supports and how much it talks.
- `src/world/clients.rs`: The clients' second: fading, walking, leaving and coming back, choosing an access point (5 GHz while it is good, roaming only once the current one is clearly worse), traffic, and renewing leases at half their time.
- `src/world/layout.rs`: Building the world from a [`SimConfig`]: the gateway and the access points at their places, then the clients dealt from the deck, settled where they would be after a while.
- `src/world/mod.rs`: [`World`]: the simulated house.
- `src/world/nodes.rs`: The nodes' second: reboots (an access point goes down and boots again, its clients move to the others), drifting load, memory and temperature, the radios' noise and air time, and the routine lines of their logs.
- `src/world/radio.rs`: Radio arithmetic: bands and channels, indoor path loss, and the rates a signal-to-noise ratio buys (MCS tables of 802.11n, ac and ax).
- `src/world/steering.rs`: Client steering where the controller asks (features/wifi.md, Steering & balancing; D-093): the agent's `btm` op has the client's access point send a BSS transition request, and an 802.11v client (the sim's WPA3 ones, whose extended capabilities say so) agrees and goes: hostapd pushes its answer as `bss-transition-response`, then the client roams. usteer, where it runs ([`Node::steers`], set from the node's disk), tells the controller where it hears a client (`get_client_info`) and no longer steers on its own: the render turns its band steering and roam triggers off.
- `src/world/tests.rs`: The world's dynamics over simulated hours: determinism, roaming, leaving, reboots.
- `src/world/traffic.rs`: Traffic: what each client downloads and uploads per second (bursty, capped by its link), the retries a weak signal costs, and the counters it moves on its access point's radio, its uplink and the gateway's WAN port.
- `tests/ban.rs`: The simulated agent's `ban` op (D-084): a banned client is kicked off the node and stays off it while banned (it may go to another access point); a lift kicks nobody, and a kick alone deauthenticates without keeping it off.
- `tests/bss.rs`: The simulated agent's `bss` op (D-083): a BSS it turns off is down in the `radios` set (netifd still lists it) and its clients are gone from `stations`; turned on, both come back; a phy the node lacks is refused.
- `tests/engine.rs`: The engine over the simulated fleet, on tokio's paused clock: the nodes come online with their facts, ticks and pushes keep them fresh, roams are inferred, logs follow, and a rebooted access point goes offline and comes back; the topology is the simulated house.
- `tests/factory.rs`: A factory-default gateway (`SimConfig::factory`; features/adoption.md, Path E): root has no password until `passwd` gives it one, and the LAN follows the gateway's `network` when its ports bounce, as the apply's make-before-break renumbering needs (D-081).
- `tests/rrm.rs`: The simulated agent's `rrm` op: each access point's own neighbor report, and lists that are set once and left alone when sent again.

### `uniwrt-store` (crates/store)

SQLite persistence: one database in WAL mode, a batching writer thread, a read pool and repositories.

- `src/codec.rs`: Column encodings shared by the repositories: enums as serde names, MACs as canonical text, timestamps as Unix milliseconds, and constraint violations as the domain errors they mean.
- `src/connection.rs`: Opening connections: the private database file, the writer's pragmas and migrations, readers.
- `src/error.rs`: Store errors: opening and migrating, domain outcomes (conflict, not found) and failed writes.
- `src/lib.rs`: SQLite persistence: one database in WAL mode, a batching writer thread, a read pool and repositories.
- `src/migrate.rs`: Forward-only schema migrations, embedded at build time and tracked in `PRAGMA user_version`.
- `src/readers.rs`: The read pool: read-only connections, opened on demand, used on tokio's blocking pool.
- `src/repo/adoption.rs`: Adopting a node in one transaction ([`NodeRepo::adopt_node`]), and [`InventoryRepo`] on SQLite: the `node_inventory` and `node_backups` tables.
- `src/repo/alerts.rs`: [`AlertRepo`] on SQLite: the `alert_rules`, `alerts` and `maintenance_windows` tables.
- `src/repo/alerts_tests.rs`: Alerts over a real database: rules and presets, the engine's writes by rule and subject, filters and pages, what the engine resumes, acknowledgements, retention, and maintenance windows.
- `src/repo/applies.rs`: [`ApplyRepo`] on SQLite: the `node_applied` table, and the nodes' addresses an apply moved.
- `src/repo/audit.rs`: [`AuditRepo`] on SQLite: the `audit` table.
- `src/repo/backhaul.rs`: [`BackhaulRepo`] on SQLite: the `backhaul_failures` table.
- `src/repo/clients.rs`: [`ClientRepo`] on SQLite: the `clients` and `client_sessions` tables.
- `src/repo/drift.rs`: [`DriftRepo`] on SQLite: the `node_config` table (what the controller confirmed, written by [`ApplyRepo::record_applied`](super::ApplyRepo::record_applied)), `config_drift` and `drift_mutes`.
- `src/repo/drift_tests.rs`: (no header comment)
- `src/repo/events.rs`: [`EventRepo`] on SQLite: the `events` table.
- `src/repo/events_tests.rs`: Events over a real database: recording and folding, filters and pages, the conditions still raised, and retention by age and count.
- `src/repo/facts.rs`: [`FactsRepo`] on SQLite: the `node_facts` table, one JSON snapshot per node.
- `src/repo/host_keys.rs`: [`HostKeyRepo`] on SQLite: the `node_host_keys` table, one pinned host key per node.
- `src/repo/jobs.rs`: [`JobRepo`] on SQLite: the `jobs` table, each job's steps and error as JSON.
- `src/repo/logs.rs`: [`LogRepo`] on SQLite: the `logs`, `logs_fts`, `log_sources` and `log_searches` tables.
- `src/repo/logs_tests.rs`: Logs over a real database: recording, filters and full-text search, pages, context, the histogram, sources, retention by age and size, and saved searches.
- `src/repo/metrics.rs`: [`MetricsRepo`] on SQLite: the `metric_series`, `metrics_raw`, `metrics_1m`, `metrics_1h` and `metric_rollups` tables.
- `src/repo/metrics_tests.rs`: Metrics over a real database: recording, rollups with their envelopes and weights, reading with tails from finer resolutions, the series catalogue, and retention.
- `src/repo/mod.rs`: Repository traits: the store's API by concern.
- `src/repo/nodes.rs`: [`NodeRepo`] on SQLite: the `nodes` table.
- `src/repo/notifiers.rs`: [`NotifierRepo`] and [`SettingsRepo`] on SQLite: the `notifiers` and `settings` tables.
- `src/repo/notifiers_tests.rs`: Notifiers and settings over a real database: created, listed, updated, deliveries recorded, deleted; a setting stored and replaced.
- `src/repo/revisions.rs`: [`RevisionRepo`] on SQLite: the `revisions` table, and the configuration secrets committed with them into `vault`.
- `src/repo/revisions_tests.rs`: Revisions over a real database: the linear history, conflicts, diffs, paging, and secrets committed with their revision and only referable from its descendants or a restore.
- `src/repo/rf.rs`: [`RfRepo`] on SQLite: the `rf_scans` table, what each scan heard as JSON.
- `src/repo/rf_tests.rs`: Scans over a real database: stored, the latest per radio, listed, read, pruned, and gone with their node.
- `src/repo/sessions.rs`: [`SessionRepo`] on SQLite: the `sessions` table.
- `src/repo/speed.rs`: [`SpeedTestRepo`] on SQLite: the `speed_tests` table.
- `src/repo/topology.rs`: [`TopologyRepo`] on SQLite: the `topology_history` and `topology_layout` tables.
- `src/repo/users.rs`: [`UserRepo`] on SQLite: the `users` table.
- `src/store.rs`: The store handle: opening with migrations, reads through the pool, writes through the writer.
- `src/testing.rs`: Test support: a fresh store in a temporary directory, on a manual clock.
- `src/vault/backup.rs`: Configuration backups, sealed like secrets: [`Vault::seal_backup`] before they are stored (with the node at adoption, [`Adoption`](crate::Adoption)), [`Vault::open_backup`] to read one back.
- `src/vault/config.rs`: Configuration secrets (features/security.md, Secrets vault): Wi-Fi passphrases, the mesh key, the PPPoE password.
- `src/vault/key.rs`: The master key: 32 random bytes that every secret in the vault is sealed under, kept outside the database (`master.key` or `UNIWRT_MASTER_KEY`; features/security.md, Secrets vault).
- `src/vault/mod.rs`: The secrets vault ([`Vault`]): [`VaultRepo`] over the `vault` table, every value sealed with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under the [`MasterKey`] (features/security.md, Secrets vault).
- `src/vault/roaming.rs`: The controller's roaming key (features/wifi.md, Roaming; D-085): 32 random bytes made on first use and kept in the vault (`controller/roaming_key`), from which each WLAN's 802.11r key is derived.
- `src/vault/seal.rs`: Sealing one secret: XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a subkey of the master key, with a random nonce and the secret's name as associated data, so a sealed value cannot be moved to another name.
- `src/vault/tests.rs`: The vault over a real database: sealing, resealing the stub's rows and refusing a wrong key.
- `src/writer.rs`: The writer: one thread owns the only write connection and commits queued operations in batches.

### `uniwrt-syslog` (crates/syslog)

Syslog: the RFC 3164/5424 parser, the UDP and TCP receiver, and the annotations that explain log entries (observability.md, Logs).

- `src/annotate.rs`: Annotations (observability.md, Logs): `data/log-patterns.toml` maps a regex over an entry's text, for some programs or all, to what it means ([`LogPattern`]).
- `src/frame.rs`: Syslog over TCP (RFC 6587): each frame is octet-counted (`LEN SP MSG`) or ends with a line feed or a NUL (non-transparent framing; logd ends its messages with `\n`, or `\0` with `log_trailer_null`).
- `src/lib.rs`: Syslog: the RFC 3164/5424 parser, the UDP and TCP receiver, and the annotations that explain log entries (observability.md, Logs).
- `src/parse.rs`: Parsing one syslog message (RFC 5424, else RFC 3164 as BSD syslog and OpenWrt's logd send it).
- `src/receiver.rs`: The receiver: syslog over UDP and TCP, each message parsed and handed on with its sender's address.

### `uniwrt-system` (crates/system)

The system harness (TESTING.md, System): rendered configs on real OpenWrt.

- `src/docker.rs`: A node of the harness: an OpenWrt container that the tests reach through `docker exec`.
- `src/lib.rs`: The system harness (TESTING.md, System): rendered configs on real OpenWrt.
- `src/site.rs`: The sites the harness renders: a new site's defaults and a home site with VLANs, each behind one of the ISP's uplinks (scripts/system/): DHCP untagged or on VLAN 201, static, or PPPoE; and the hwsim lab's site (scripts/wifi-lab.sh), whose WLAN and mesh client c knows.
- `tests/apply/dial.rs`: A [`Dial`] over `docker exec`: the controller's logins to the harness's containers.
- `tests/apply/main.rs`: End-to-end applies (TESTING.md, System; D-070) on scripts/test-system.sh's topology, `isp ═ gw ═ ap`: the controller's apply job reaches the gateway and the AP over a `docker exec` dial ([`dial`]), turns management on (installing the transaction tool and the guard), and applies revisions through the real tool, agent and health checks: a confirmed apply, a broken WAN that rolls both back (alone, when more than the WAN changes: D-081), a lost AP that rolls back at its deadline, and the LAN renumbered make-before-break under a host behind the gateway.
- `tests/steering.rs`: Steering's usteer (D-090) on the hwsim lab: node a (25.12, apk) and node b (24.10, opkg) install usteer from the feeds, take the `usteer` package rendered for the lab site with the Balanced profile, and run it: each reads back the profile's thresholds and the steered SSID (`get_config`), steers its access points of that SSID (`local_info`), and hears the other's over the LAN (`remote_info`), and a's usteer places client c on its access point (`get_client_info`, as the controller's steering reads it).
- `tests/system.rs`: Rendered configs on OpenWrt (TESTING.md, System), on scripts/test-system.sh's topology: `isp ═ gw ═ ap`.
- `tests/wifi.rs`: Rendered Wi-Fi and mesh on the hwsim lab (TESTING.md, System; scripts/wifi-lab.sh): node a becomes the gateway and node b the AP of [`site::lab`], and client c must lease again on both bands. b's 5 GHz uplink reaches a's DHCP server only through the mesh: b is cut off Docker's network for the test, so its frames cross `bat0`, tagged with labnet's VLAN.
- `tests/wifi/backhaul.rs`: The wired backhaul on the lab's cable (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-094): `bh0`, a veth pair between a (25.12) and b (24.10), comes over as the apply stages it.
- `tests/wpad.rs`: The wpad swap's commands (D-089) on the hwsim lab (TESTING.md, Wi-Fi lab), as the job runs them: node a (25.12, apk) and node b (24.10, opkg) get the basic wpad first, then the swap downloads both wpads, loses the route to the feeds, and swaps offline.

### `uniwrt-topo` (crates/topo)

The topology: the network graph that the adopted nodes' facts describe.

- `src/clients.rs`: Who clients are (names and addresses from the DHCP leases and the neighbor caches), and the last way to place one: a node that has it in its neighbor cache, off its uplink.
- `src/diff.rs`: What changed between two builds, by id: the WS topic sends it instead of the whole graph.
- `src/fleet.rs`: Who is who: the adopted nodes ([`Member`]s) in build order, the MAC addresses each one owns, the vertex ids, and lookups in a node's facts.
- `src/graph.rs`: The topology graph: what [`build`](crate::build) returns, the API serves and the WS topic `topology` keeps current.
- `src/history.rs`: What the topology's history keeps of a build, for the replay (features/observability.md, Topology): its shape, states and link quality, without what changes at every build.
- `src/lib.rs`: The topology: the network graph that the adopted nodes' facts describe.
- `src/links.rs`: The graph while it is built: vertices by id, and links by key, each merged from every end that reports it.
- `src/mesh.rs`: The mesh: 802.11s peer links and batman-adv neighbors (over Wi-Fi a mesh link, over Ethernet a wired one), batman-adv's best paths toward the gateway, and the clients its translation tables place.
- `src/quality.rs`: Link quality on one 0–100 scale, whatever measures it, and traffic rates between builds.
- `src/tests/build.rs`: A whole build: the WAN, the fallback to neighbor caches, traffic rates between builds, deltas, and determinism.
- `src/tests/history.rs`: What the history keeps of a build: its shape, without traffic and load.
- `src/tests/mesh.rs`: The mesh: 802.11s and batman-adv links merged, batman-adv's best paths, peers that are not adopted, and the clients the translation tables place.
- `src/tests/mod.rs`: Topologies of scenarios built in code (`scenario.rs`), one file per source of links.
- `src/tests/scenario.rs`: Facts built in code, as small as each case needs.
- `src/tests/wifi.rs`: Wi-Fi clients at their access point, and a bridge at the access point it is a station of.
- `src/tests/wired.rs`: Wired links from the bridges' forwarding databases: cables, daisy chains, unmanaged switches.
- `src/tree.rs`: Finishing a build: the tree view (the cheapest path from the roots to every vertex, where batman-adv's best paths, wires and a WAN are cheap and links that are down dear), every edge oriented downstream, and traffic rates against the previous build.
- `src/wan.rs`: The internet and each gateway's links to it: its interfaces with a default route, or named like OpenWrt's WAN (`wan`, `wan6`, `wanb`), one link per device beneath them.
- `src/wifi.rs`: Wi-Fi: each client at the access point it is associated with (the one it used last, while it roams), and nodes that are another node's stations (a bridge's uplink).
- `src/wired.rs`: Wired links from the bridges' forwarding databases.

### `uniwrt-uci` (crates/uci)

UCI, OpenWrt's configuration format (docs/openwrt/REFERENCE.md, UCI syntax): the AST of a package, a parser and a serializer that agree with libuci, and the semantic diff that the review screen, transactions and drift detection read (features/lifecycle.md).

- `src/ast.rs`: The AST: a package of sections, each a type, an optional name and its options in order.
- `src/diff/align.rs`: Pairing the old package's sections with the new one's, and finding the ones that moved.
- `src/diff/apply.rs`: Applying a diff to the package it was taken from: `apply(a, &diff(a, b))` is `b` up to the diff's semantics (the order between types and among a section's options may differ).
- `src/diff/mod.rs`: The semantic diff of two versions of a package: which sections came, went, changed or moved, and how each option changed.
- `src/diff/show.rs`: A diff as text, in `uci show`'s terms: a line per section and per option, `+` for what came, `-` for what went, and a context line, starting with a space, for a changed section.
- `src/diff/tests.rs`: (no header comment)
- `src/lib.rs`: UCI, OpenWrt's configuration format (docs/openwrt/REFERENCE.md, UCI syntax): the AST of a package, a parser and a serializer that agree with libuci, and the semantic diff that the review screen, transactions and drift detection read (features/lifecycle.md).
- `src/name.rs`: UCI identifiers, as libuci checks them (`uci_validate_str` in util.c, ASCII in the C locale).
- `src/parse/mod.rs`: The parser: a port of libuci's (file.c, strict mode, as `uci` and rpcd run it), so text reads here as on a node, quirks included. libuci parses each line in place in a buffer, and some outcomes depend on that: a `;` glued to an unquoted word ends the line, while after a quoted part it separates statements.
- `src/parse/port.rs`: The port of libuci's parser: its buffer, positions and steps, function by function.
- `src/tests/conformance.rs`: The fixtures against what `uci` printed for them (`scripts/uci-conformance.sh` writes the `.out` files and checks that each fixture is listed here).
- `src/tests/mod.rs`: (no header comment)
- `src/tests/props.rs`: Properties: what validates round-trips through text; any text either fails or parses into a package that round-trips; a diff is empty exactly when two packages mean the same, and applying it to the old package gives the new one.
- `src/write.rs`: The serializer: text as `uci commit` writes it (libuci's `uci_export_package`), so a file the controller renders is byte for byte the file `uci` would write after a commit.

## Node agent (`node-agent`)

ucode modules, embedded in the binary and installed on nodes by hash (`crates/node/src/bundle.rs`). The entry point is `main.uc`.

- `ban.uc`: The `ban` op (features/wifi.md, Client actions; D-084): keeps clients off every access point of the node, or lets them back, through hostapd's `del_client` on each BSS (`hostapd.<ifname>`).
- `bss.uc`: The `bss` op (features/wifi.md, WLANs; D-083): turns a phy's BSSes off and on again without touching UCI, through hostapd's own `config_set`. hostapd takes the phy's config as netifd wrote it (/var/run/hostapd-<phy>[.<radio>].conf), less the BSSes named off, and adds and removes BSSes to match: the others keep running, the first BSS included (the next one takes its place), and a config without BSSes removes hostapd's interface on the phy (a mesh point there stays).
- `btm.uc`: The `btm` op (features/wifi.md, Steering & balancing: controller-sent transition requests; D-091, D-093): asks one client to move, with an 802.11v BSS transition request from the access point it is connected to (hostapd's `bss_transition_request` on `hostapd.<ifname>`).
- `bus.uc`: ubus calls on one shared connection, with errors mapped to the protocol's codes.
- `collect.uc`: The collect sets: each gathers the raw sources of one part of the node's facts, which crates/node/src/facts parses.
- `collect/batman.uc`: The `batman` set: each batman-adv mesh device as batctl's JSON queries report it: the mesh, its hard interfaces, originators, neighbors, gateways and both translation tables.
- `collect/board.uc`: The `board` set: what the node is (`system board`, the release file and board.json).
- `collect/capabilities.uc`: The `capabilities` set: features detected on the node, never inferred from its version: the package manager, optional software, what hostapd and wpa_supplicant were built with, and how the switch is driven.
- `collect/config.uc`: The `config` set: the SHA-256 of each UCI package in /etc/config, for drift detection (features/lifecycle.md, Drift).
- `collect/devices.uc`: The `devices` set: every kernel network device, from sysfs, with the counters of /proc/net/dev.
- `collect/interfaces.uc`: The `interfaces` set: netifd's logical interfaces (`network.interface dump`).
- `collect/leases.uc`: The `leases` set: DHCP leases from dnsmasq's lease files (each `dnsmasq` section's `leasefile`, /tmp/dhcp.leases by default) and from odhcpd over ubus (`dhcp ipv6leases`, and `ipv4leases` where odhcpd serves DHCPv4), with the node's clock, which dnsmasq's expiry times are on; and miniupnpd's lease file (`upnpd.config.upnp_lease_file`), the ports clients opened, where miniupnpd is set up.
- `collect/neighbors.uc`: The `neighbors` set: the IPv4 and IPv6 neighbor caches and the bridges' forwarding databases.
- `collect/phys.uc`: The `phys` set: the radio hardware (nl80211 `GET_WIPHY`) per band: its channels with their regulatory flags and power limits, and its HT, VHT, HE and EHT capabilities.
- `collect/radios.uc`: The `radios` set: each radio's configuration and state from netifd (`network.wireless status`), the phys' interfaces from nl80211 (`GET_INTERFACE`), and the survey of each phy's channel with the share of time it was busy since the previous collection. netifd's reply holds the Wi-Fi keys, so only the options that facts use are kept.
- `collect/stations.uc`: The `stations` set: the stations of every Wi-Fi interface (nl80211 `GET_STATION`): an AP's clients, mesh peers and a station interface's AP, with signal, rates, counters and airtime; and for APs, the capabilities hostapd saw in each client's association (`get_clients`).
- `collect/system.uc`: The `system` set: resource usage (`system info`), the node's clock, CPU load since the previous collection and the thermal sensors.
- `exec.uc`: Commands as argv arrays, never shell strings, with a timeout and bounded output.
- `logs.uc`: Following the node's log (`log_follow`; event loop only), pushed as `{"ev":"log",…}` events in batches.
- `main.uc`: The uniwrt node agent: serves the controller's requests from stdin and answers on stdout, one JSON object per line (proto.uc), until stdin closes.
- `mtu.uc`: The `mtu` op (features/mesh.md, Wired backhaul; D-094): whether a cable carries packets of `size` bytes, batman-adv's 1532 on a backhaul's VLAN device (`<port>.<vid>`).
- `ops.uc`: The agent's operations (`proto::ops`).
- `proto.uc`: The agent protocol, mirrored from crates/node/src/proto.rs and proto/ops.rs: one JSON object per line in each direction.
- `rrm.uc`: The `rrm` op (features/wifi.md, Roaming): 802.11k neighbor reports.
- `scan.uc`: The `scan` op's worker, run by ops.uc as a process of its own (`ucode scan.uc '<args>'`) so that its nl80211 socket is its own: a forked task would share the agent's, and the agent's ticks could read the scan's replies.
- `streams.uc`: Push events from ubus (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`; event loop only): the notifications of daemons' objects, forwarded as `{"ev":"<source>.<type>","ts":…,"data":{…}}` with the data as the daemon sent it.
- `ticks.uc`: Periodic collection (`set_interval`; event loop only): sets collected on a schedule and pushed as `{"tick":{"sets":{…},"errors":{…}}}`, the shape of a `collect` answer.
- `util.uc`: Small helpers shared by the agent's modules: readers of files, sysfs attributes and shell-variable files, `pick`, and clocks.
- `wifi.uc`: Shared by the Wi-Fi sets: the kernel phys from sysfs, and nl80211 (ucode-mod-nl80211, which hostapd depends on), loaded on first use because images without Wi-Fi lack it.

## Scripts

- `scripts/arch-check.sh`: Enforces the layering rules (`just arch-check`; `just check` and CI run it):   - each crate depends only on the crates that docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's table ("Crates and     layering") allows, read from the doc itself so the two cannot drift; dev-dependencies may     also use the test crates, whose own dev-dependencies are free;   - L0 crates have no async runtime, socket, database or SSH crate in their dependency tree,     and their source does no IO and reads no clock (CONVENTIONS.md, Architecture rules); a     line marked `arch-check: allow` is exempt, with the reason beside the marker;   - in web/src, features never import other features, ui/ imports only lib/strings from     outside itself, lib/ imports only api/, viz/ only ui/, lib/ and api/, and only a     feature's tests import app/;   - no two Rust types export one TypeScript name (ts-rs would write both to one file).
- `scripts/arch-check.test.sh`: Tests scripts/arch-check.sh against a small fixture workspace, one violation per case; `just check` and CI run it.
- `scripts/check.sh`: Runs everything CI gates on, one line per step (`just check`).
- `scripts/cross.sh`: Builds static musl binaries with cargo-zigbuild inside its container, so the host needs only Docker.
- `scripts/gen-map.sh`: Regenerates docs/MAP.md, the code map: each Rust file with the first sentence of its `//!` header, the web UI's directories and the scripts.
- `scripts/new-feature.sh`: Scaffolds a feature area along the feature recipe (CONVENTIONS.md), steps 2–6, wired in and compiling, with TODO(new-feature) markers where the real work goes (`just new-feature`):   model      crates/model/src/<mod>.rs, a type deriving TS behind the `ts` feature   api        crates/api/src/<mod>.rs, GET /api/v1/<area> answering a DTO that derives TS   web        web/src/features/<area>/<Pascal>Page.tsx and its test, the lazy route of a page              in app/nav.ts, the client in lib/api.ts and the strings in lib/strings.ts   telemetry  (--telemetry) node-agent/collect/<mod>.uc, its parser in crates/node/src/facts/              and a fixture; the steps that make it a collect set are printed Render (step 3) is skipped until crates/render exists.
- `scripts/new-feature.test.sh`: Tests scripts/new-feature.sh (`just test-new-feature`; CI's rust job runs it): scaffolds an area with telemetry in a throwaway worktree that mirrors the working tree, then holds the result to what CI gates on (clippy, the new tests, the web checks, arch-check), and checks that a second run refuses to write.
- `scripts/next-version.sh`: Prints the next release version from the Conventional Commits since the last vX.Y.Z tag (D-008), or nothing when HEAD is already released.
- `scripts/next-version.test.sh`: Tests scripts/next-version.sh against throwaway git repositories; `just check` and CI run it.
- `scripts/oui.py`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/system-node.Dockerfile`: An OpenWrt rootfs for the system harness (scripts/test-system.sh): the stock image plus `bridge`, to check the bridge's VLANs, a PPPoE server and client, for the ISP's end, and sqm-scripts, mwan3 and miniupnpd (off, as an install leaves them before a transaction turns them on), to check what render writes for SQM, failover (D-076) and UPnP (D-079).
- `scripts/system/isp.uci`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/system/pap-secrets`: The subscriber the harness dials in as (crates/system/src/site.rs).
- `scripts/system/pppoe-server-options`: The ISP's PPP options (scripts/test-system.sh): PAP against pap-secrets, not system accounts.
- `scripts/test-agent.sh`: Runs the agent tests against OpenWrt booted with procd (TESTING.md, Agent): for each OpenWrt rootfs image, boots a container with a random root password and runs crates/node/tests/agent.rs, crates/engine/tests/agent.rs and crates/jobs/tests/agent.rs against it, then crates/node/tests/txn.rs one test at a time (transactions change the node), the boot test last (it restarts the container).
- `scripts/test-dropbear.sh`: Runs the transport tests against dropbear on real OpenWrt (TESTING.md, Transport): for each OpenWrt rootfs image, starts a container with a random root password and one without (factory defaults) and runs crates/node/tests/dropbear.rs against them.
- `scripts/test-system.sh`: The system harness (TESTING.md, System): rendered configs on real OpenWrt.
- `scripts/tz.py`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/uci-conformance.sh`: The uci crate's conformance fixtures (TESTING.md, Fixtures): runs `uci export` on every fixture in crates/uci/fixtures/{cases,openwrt/*} inside OpenWrt rootfs containers, requires the releases to agree, and writes what uci printed next to each fixture as <name>.out (its stdout when it succeeded, else its error).
- `scripts/wifi-lab.sh`: The hwsim lab (TESTING.md, Wi-Fi lab): OpenWrt nodes with virtual radios (mac80211_hwsim) and a batman-adv mesh, in containers booted with procd.
- `scripts/wifi-lab/a/setup.uci`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-lab/a/wireless`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-lab/b/setup.uci`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-lab/b/wireless`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-lab/c/setup.uci`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-lab/c/wireless`: (no header comment)
- `scripts/wifi-node.Dockerfile`: An OpenWrt rootfs with the Wi-Fi and batman-adv user space, for the hwsim lab (scripts/wifi-lab.sh), and `bridge` for the system harness's checks.
